scope: Proposition 9.4 (Averaged two-sweep contraction) of the manuscript “Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps” (preprints/Conditional-information-under-deterministic-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ad4125b0a60530a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the initial ordered card list uniformly and independently of all switches. Fix an exposure index with m ≥ εn available positions, where ε = 1/q and q is a fixed power of two. Put b = ⌊d/2⌋ and ∆n = 2n(n + 1) exp[−ε(1/2 − e−1 )2b ]. At sweep boundaries t, the tag process obeys EEt+2d ≤ ∆n + h (1 + b/2)(1 − ε/4)d−b + 2−b i EEt. (9.5) With q = 128, R = 128q, and T = 2Rd, EET ≤ n−8 + R∆n. Consequently the average endpoint TV distance of an ordered list of n − n/q cards tends to zero.
